# A simplex contraction identity and all-dimensional boundary-potential sharpness

This note proves an exact convex-order identity, and applies it to the full
nonnegative convex-potential cone on the sharp binary-times-simplex family.
It does not prove that an arbitrary critical circuit has the required
individual efficiency.

## 1. Uniform simplex measure dominates a mixture of vertex contractions

Let T have m affinely independent vertices v_1,...,v_m, let mu be its
normalized (m−1)-dimensional volume, and set alpha=m/(m+1). For every
continuous convex function f on T,

    (1/m) sum_j integral_T f(alpha x+(1−alpha)v_j) dmu(x)
        <= integral_T f(x) dmu(x).                         (1)

For m=1 both sides are f(v_1). Suppose m>=2. Write lambda_j for the
barycentric coordinates. The probability measures with densities
m lambda_j relative to mu have average mu, because sum_j lambda_j=1.
We prove (1) by comparing the j-th contracted uniform measure with this
j-th tilted measure.

Fix j. A uniform point of T is uniquely expressible, outside null sets, as

    X=(1-R)v_j+R Z,

where Z is uniform on the opposite facet, R and Z are independent, and
R has density (m−1)r^(m−2) on [0,1]. This follows directly by parametrizing
the simplex as a cone over the opposite facet: the cross section at r
has (m−2)-volume proportional to r^(m−2). It also holds for m=2, when Z
is the single opposite vertex. Tilting by m lambda_j=m(1-r) leaves the
conditional law of Z unchanged and gives radial density

    a(r)=m(m−1) r^(m−2)(1−r),             0<=r<=1.

The contracted point alpha X+(1−alpha)v_j has the same direction Z and
radial density

    b(r)=(m−1) alpha^(−(m−1)) r^(m−2) 1_[0,alpha](r).

Both densities integrate to one. Their means, by elementary integration,
are both (m−1)/(m+1). On (0,alpha), their difference has the sign of

    m(1-r)−alpha^(−(m−1)).

Its unique zero is q=1−alpha^(−(m−1))/m. It lies strictly between zero
and alpha. Indeed Bernoulli's inequality gives

    m alpha^(m−1) >= 2m/(m+1)>1,

so q>0, while m(1−alpha)=alpha<alpha^(−(m−1)) gives q<alpha.
Above alpha the difference is strictly positive. Thus a−b has signs
positive, negative, positive on (0,q), (q,alpha), (alpha,1).

For any convex continuous g on [0,1], let L be the affine function through
(q,g(q)) and (alpha,g(alpha)). Convexity gives g−L nonnegative outside
[q,alpha] and nonpositive inside. Consequently

    integral (g−L)(a−b) >= 0.

The integral of L(a−b) vanishes because the masses and means agree.
Hence integral g b <= integral g a. Apply this to
g(r)=f((1-r)v_j+rZ), for every fixed Z, and integrate in Z. It proves that
the j-th contracted uniform measure is dominated for convex tests by the
measure with density m lambda_j. Averaging over j proves (1).

All integrations are finite, on compact sets, with bounded continuous
integrands. The cone parametrization and mixture identities specify the
measures explicitly; no compactness or existence of an optimizing test is
used.

## 2. The exact simplex-facet profile inequality

Let K be a d-dimensional simplex, d>=1, with barycentric coordinates
lambda_0,...,lambda_d. Put alpha=d/(d+1), Gamma=alpha^d, and

    W(x)=(1/(d+1)) sum_(j=0)^d 1_{lambda_j(x)>=1/(d+1)}.

For each facet F and every continuous convex f on F,

    integral_F f W dH_(d−1) <= Gamma integral_F f dH_(d−1).   (2)

For d=1, each facet is one endpoint, precisely one barycentric coordinate
is one, and W=1/2=Gamma there; this uses counting measure H_0 directly.

For d>=2, the facet opposite vertex r has lambda_r=0 and is a simplex
with m=d vertices. The subset lambda_j>=1/(d+1) on that facet is exactly
alpha F+(1−alpha)v_j. Its measure Jacobian is alpha^(d−1). Thus the left
side of (2) equals

    alpha^(d−1)/(d+1) sum_(j!=r)
        integral_F f(alpha x+(1−alpha)v_j) dH_(d−1)(x).

Apply (1) with m=d. The resulting coefficient is
d alpha^(d−1)/(d+1)=alpha^d=Gamma, proving (2).

The inequality allows signed convex f. It holds separately on each facet,
so each facet may also carry its own nonnegative constant weight. In
particular it applies to nonnegative normal-dependent physical potentials:
on each facet the outward normal is fixed and the restriction in x is
convex. Facet intersections have H_(d−1)-measure zero when d>=2.

## 3. Exact efficiencies on the mixed binary product

Let P={0,1}^n, including P={0} in the zero-dimensional base convention,
let N=2^n, and let S=P times K. Its ambient convex hull is the full body
[0,1]^n times K when n+d>=1. Here d>=1, so its intrinsic measure is
mixed d-volume. Let eta be the sum of the fiber boundary measures,
with outward normals attached when normal-dependent tests are used.
Its total is N times the positive finite surface measure B of K.

For p in P define the affine function

    L_p(z)=sum_l [(1-p_l)z_l+p_l(1-z_l)].

On the measured bases it is their Hamming distance from p. The d+1 caps

    H_(p,j)={lambda_j(x)−1/(d+1)−L_p(z)>=0}                 (3)

strictly miss every other fiber and are the centroid vertex caps on p.
Their raw masses are all Gamma vol_d(K). Their continuous normals are
the gradients of the barycentric functions and sum to zero. Differentiating
the exact formula vol{lambda_j>=t}=(1-t)^d vol_d(K) at t=1/(d+1) shows
that all their coarea section measures are
d alpha^(d−1) vol_d(K)>0. Hence their regular circuit weights are exactly
1/(d+1). Their section centroids equal the simplex centroid, since the
fixed barycentric coordinate is 1/(d+1) and each of the other d centroid
coordinates is alpha/d=1/(d+1).

Let W_p be the resulting boundary profile. It is the W of Section 2 on
the p-fiber and zero elsewhere. Applying (2) facetwise gives, for every
nonnegative admissible convex physical potential Phi,

    integral Phi W_p deta <= Gamma integral_(boundary K_p) Phi deta.

The same statement holds for normal-dependent potentials convex in the
physical variables at each fixed normal. Summing in p and dividing by
any positive total denominator proves

    min_p [integral Phi W_p deta / integral Phi deta] <= Gamma/N.  (4)

Individually each profile has efficiency at most Gamma. Both bounds are
attained: the nonnegative convex base hinge

    phi_p(z,x)=(1−L_p(z))_+

equals one on fiber p and zero on all other measured fibers. By (2) with
the constant test, whose inequality is an equality in (1), its individual
ratio is exactly Gamma. The sum over all p is one on every measured
fiber, and each W_p integral is Gamma B. Its common ratio is Gamma/N.
This proves the exact individual and common suprema, without an unproved
attainment assertion.

These are the actual globally critical simplex circuits: their caps cover
each own fiber, giving the upper bound Gamma/N for mixed depth; the
ordinary simplex centroid inequality gives the matching lower bound at
each fiber centroid. The latter ordinary inequality is independently
proved in the archived central-simplex depth theorem. The new assertion
here is the sharp bound over the ENTIRE convex-potential cone, including
normal-dependent convex tests, and its explicit attainment by base hinges.

The d=0 counting example uses no boundary-potential measure and is not
treated by this surface argument. No inequality for arbitrary mixed-
integer fibers or arbitrary critical profiles follows from this calibration.
